correctness.rationale: For every integer n>=3 the optimization fixes constant Fourier coefficient one and allows real a,b,c with continuous-circle nonnegativity. Q=1+sqrt(2)cosθ+(1/2)cos2θ=(cosθ+1/sqrt(2))^2 is feasible and vanishes at 3pi/4 and 5pi/4. If n≡2 mod4 then cos(nθ) vanishes at both contacts, so T(3pi/4)=1-a/sqrt(2)>=0 and a<=sqrt(2). Otherwise gamma=cos(3pi n/4)≠0; the perturbation P_n=cosθ+2sgn(gamma)cos(nθ) is positive at both contacts with value -1/sqrt(2)+2|gamma|>=1/sqrt(2). Continuity provides strictly positive P_n near the finite contact set, while Q has positive compact minimum on its complement; sufficiently small ε>0 makes Q+εP_n nonnegative everywhere and gives a=sqrt(2)+ε. Exact symbolic checks confirmed the square and m=2 specialization; symbolic residue checking over n=3..80 corroborates the contact sign. These finite tests are not the universal proof.

value.rationale: The fixed degree-two sparse-support extremal problem is a classical, natural object, and the exact infinite mod-four classification answers a meaningful equality-versus-strict-improvement boundary for the effect of any one extra harmonic. Its precise resonance information can be used as a sharp support-design criterion even without strict-case exact constants. This independent utility does not restore originality: as a standalone contribution the result is already implicit in an available general contact-resonance construction and thus rejected despite the useful statement.
